ripis: rīpa, -ae (f.) — bank of a river (abl./dat. pl.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rumpit: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst; break silence with (3rd sg. pres.)
rutuli: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, people of Turnus in Latium (nom. pl.); Rutulus, -ī, a Rutulian (gen. sg.) · also m. voc. pl. (O Rutuli)
rutulis: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Rutulians, people of Latium under Turnus (dat./abl. pl.)
ruunt: ruō, ruere, ruī — to rush, tumble; trans. to churn up, upheave (3rd pl. pres.)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl. · also f. nom. sg. (dea saeva)
satis: satis (indecl. n., adv.) — enough, sufficient; adv., sufficiently
saxea: saxeus, -a, -um — of stone, rocky, stony (n. acc. pl.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedens: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
sequuntur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (3rd pl. pres., deponent)
serena: serēnus, -a, -um — clear, cloudless, calm (f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
similis: similis, -e — like, similar (+ gen./dat.) (m./f. nom. sg.; f. acc. pl. in -is)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
sollemnia: sollemnis, -e — yearly, solemn, ritual; sollemnia (n. pl.), rites, ceremonies (n. acc./nom. pl.)
solum: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, soil, land (acc./nom. sg.); also sōlus, alone (n. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (sōlus, alone: hoc sōlum nōmen) · also adv., only, merely
sonantem: sonō, -āre, -uī, -itum — to sound, ring, resound (pres. part., m. acc. sg.) · also f. acc. sg. (turbam sonantem)
sonat: sonō, -āre, sonuī, sonitum — to sound, resound, give forth (3rd sg. pres.)
spirantis: spīrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to breathe, breathe out (pres. part., m. acc. pl., -is for -ēs; also m./f./n. gen. sg.)
spumantem: spūmō, -āre — to foam, froth (pres. part., f. acc. sg.)
sternit: sternō, sternere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, strew, spread (3rd sg. pres.)
sternitur: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, strew, stretch out (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
stridens: strīdō, strīdere — to hiss, shriek, whistle (pres. part., f. nom. sg.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
succedunt: succēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go up to, advance upon, approach (3rd pl. pres.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
superbis: superbus, -a, -um — proud, splendid, lordly (n. abl. pl.) · also f. abl. pl. (ratibus superbīs, 'proud ships'; m./f./n. dat./abl. pl.)
superbos: superbus, -a, -um — proud, haughty; superbī, the proud (m. acc. pl., used as noun)
supplex: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, begging humbly (nom. sg.)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talis: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) · also m./f. nom. sg. (talis erat Dido)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
telis: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (abl./dat. pl.)
telum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, arrow, weapon (acc./nom. sg.)
templa: templum, -ī (n.) — temple, sanctuary, sacred precinct (acc./nom. pl.)
tempora: tempus, temporis (n.) — time, season, occasion (acc. pl.) · also tempora, -um (n. pl.), temples of the head (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl.
tenuem: tenuis, -e — thin, slender, fine (m./f. acc. sg.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tollunt: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise; se tollere, to rise up (3rd pl. pres.)
torquent: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl (3rd pl. pres.)
torquet: torqueō, torquēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd sg. pres.)
totis: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n. abl. pl., with tectis)
trahit: trahō, -ere, trāxī, tractum — to drag, draw along (3 sg. pres.)
tremit: tremō, -ere, -uī — to tremble, quake, shake (3rd sg. pres.)
troes: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. pl., Greek form Trōes)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) · also f. abl./dat. pl. (tuīs querēlīs)
tulit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, bring, carry; sē ferre, to betake oneself (3rd sg. perf.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
veniens: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come, approach (pres. part., m./f./n. nom. sg.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
ventura: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; ventūrus, about to come; ventūra (n. pl.), things to come (fut. part., n. acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (progeniēs … ventūra)
verberat: verberō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to lash, beat, strike (3rd sg. pres.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vertitur: vertō, vertere, vertī, versum — to turn; vertitur, wheels round (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
videbat: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. impf.)
videre: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (pres. inf.) · also 3rd pl. perf. (= vīdērunt)
virtutem: virtūs, virtūtis (f.) — manliness, courage, valour (acc. sg.)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
